extracted.intended_audience: AISTATS 2022 reviewers (peer reviewers of conference submissions)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for reviewing machine learning / statistics submissions to AISTATS 2022, covering what to evaluate (correctness, novelty, clarity, reproducibility, impact), how to score and provide constructive feedback, and procedural/confidentiality requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the review
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the review process is twofold: identify papers which offer significant contributions to the fields of artificial intelligence and statistics, and provide constructive feedback to authors to improve their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing, always think about the long-run impact: out-of-the-box ideas, novel problems, and 'bridging fields' contributions are crucial. Novel or interdisciplinary works may be easy to criticize due to community unfamiliarity; avoid dismissive criticism and be aware of bias against nonstandard approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary and contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly summarize the paper, its motivation, key contributions and achievements in a paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This helps ACs and program chairs and can reveal misunderstandings to authors. Summaries are invaluable even if they provide little new information to authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the strengths of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical criteria include soundness of claims (theoretical grounding, empirical evaluation), significance and novelty, and relevance to the AISTATS community. Cite relevant prior works when comparing novelty or significance. Consider the likelihood that researchers/practitioners will use or be influenced by the proposed ideas. Solid technical papers that explore new territory or point to new research directions are preferable to incremental improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the limitations of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on limitations of soundness (theory, empirical), significance/novelty, and relevance. Comments should be detailed, specific, and polite—avoid vague, subjective complaints. Do not review based on your personal interest level but on scientific contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correctness
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the claims and method correct? Is the empirical methodology correct?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain any incorrectness. Incorrect claims or methodology are the primary reason for rejection. Be detailed, specific and polite, and thoroughly motivate your criticism so authors can understand and respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the paper clearly written? Does it clearly state its contributions, notation and results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess organization and whether the submission adequately informs the reader. If not clear, provide constructive suggestions for improvement. A well-written paper provides enough information for an expert reader to reproduce its results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Is it clearly discussed how this work differs from or relates to prior work in the literature?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain whether the submission shows due scholarship and suitably relates to prior work. The related work section should not just list items, but explain how the proposed work differs, builds upon, or improves prior work. Authors are not expected to know all non-peer-reviewed work; works appearing less than two months before deadline are considered concurrent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional comments (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional comments, feedback and suggestions for improvement, and any further questions for the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optional field for constructive suggestions and extra questions the reviewer might have.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there enough details to reproduce the main results of this work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the paper and supplementary materials provide sufficient information for reproduction. Lack of reproducibility should be listed among the paper's weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assumptions and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper explicitly and clearly state the main assumptions and limitations of the work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If assumptions and limitations are not clearly stated in the paper or supplement, consider listing this as a weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Societal impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper discuss the societal impact of the work, including impact from misuse of the contribution?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the paper discusses potential societal impact. If the topic warrants it and the paper lacks discussion, indicate that it should include such consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code release promise
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the authors promise to release code for this submission?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark 'Yes' if the paper promises to release code (anonymized link or included in supplementary). Accepted papers promising code will be accepted conditionally on public release by camera-ready deadline; reviewers help identify such papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall score (1-10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Score for the submission should reflect your assessment of the submission's contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Do NOT assume assigned sample is representative; do not adjust scores to match acceptance rates. Numeric scale with label guidance:
1: Trivial or wrong or already known results
2: Strong reject (I would be very upset if accepted)
3: Clear reject (I vote and argue for rejection)
4: Reject (an ok submission but not good enough)
5: Marginally below the acceptance threshold (I lean towards rejection but would not be upset if accepted)
6: Marginally above the acceptance threshold (I lean towards acceptance but would not be upset if rejected)
7: Accept (a good submission)
8: Clear accept (a very good submission, top 50% of accepted AISTATS papers)
9: Strong accept (an excellent submission, top 15% of accepted AISTATS papers)
10: Must accept (top 5% of accepted AISTATS papers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence score (1-5)
rubrics_metrics.description: How certain are you about your assessment?
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Scale definitions:
5: Absolutely certain; very familiar with related work.
4: Confident but not absolute; unlikely you misunderstood parts or are unfamiliar with some work.
3: Fairly confident; possible you misunderstood parts; math/details not carefully checked.
2: Willing to defend assessment but quite likely you did not understand central parts or are unfamiliar; details not carefully checked.
1: Educated guess; submission not in your area or difficult to understand; math/details not checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical concerns flag
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the submission raise potential ethical concerns? (Yes/No) These include methods, applications or data that create or reinforce unfair biases or have primary purpose of harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rating should be independent of your accept/reject rating. If 'Yes', briefly explain potential ethical concerns in the provided field so paper may receive additional ethical review if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of conduct agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agree to abide by the AISTATS code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must follow the AISTATS Code of Conduct during the review process (link provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must keep the paper and supplementary materials (including code and LaTeX source), as well as the reviews, confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes deleting any submitted code at the end of the review cycle to comply with confidentiality. Do not divulge author identities if accidentally discovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential comments to Area Chair (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional confidential comments field for the Area Chair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for explicit comparisons to other submissions or blunt criticisms you prefer not to share with authors. If you accidentally learn author identities, do not divulge them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best practices for tone and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: High-level reviewer behavior expectations: be thoughtful, be fair, be useful, be specific, be flexible, be timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be thoughtful: consider authors may be junior. Be fair: avoid personal biases. Be useful: provide reviews helpful to authors, reviewers, and ACs. Be specific: avoid vague statements. Be flexible: update reviews if new information emerges during discussion. Be timely: respect deadlines; notify AC if you cannot complete review on time. If pressured to provide positive/negative review, notify Program Chairs; if noticing unethical behavior, notify Area Chair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling minor formatting issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor formatting issues (e.g., citation styles, fonts) should not cause desk-rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disregard minor formatting issues in scoring (flag them but do not change score/evaluation). Conference staff will ensure correct style for camera-ready versions if accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary materials handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Some authors include extra pages or do not split supplementary materials from main paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These papers are kept in the review process. Treat extra pages as supplementary materials. Looking at supplementary materials is optional for evaluation as per the CfP.

rubrics_metrics.name: External links in submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions may contain links (URLs) to external materials such as code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers cannot guarantee the safety of external links. General recommendation: do not follow such links and treat them as statements that authors will make materials available if accepted. If you access a link, be aware it might reveal you consulted it and thus reveal involvement in review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing anonymous GitHub code
rubrics_metrics.description: Some papers may submit code (including anonymous GitHub links) as supplementary material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewing additional information such as code is optional. When accessing anonymous GitHub links, directly download or clone after logging out of your GitHub account; do NOT fork the repository to avoid revealing your identity. Note that submitted code may contain security vulnerabilities.
